issue: Compels overcoming a nonreliance clause by a legally incomplete integration-clause argument.
basis: MSA §14.1 expressly disclaims reliance on extracontractual statements. SodexoMAGIC distinguishes bare integration from integration-plus/nonreliance; latter blocks proof of justifiable reliance on prior representations. Toy is not general authority that fraudulent inducement defeats this clause. Advocacy can preserve exceptions or distinguish contractual warranties, but rubric must accept a reasoned conclusion this fraud theory cannot win summary judgment.
repair: Reward distinction between bare integration and explicit nonreliance, and allow narrowing relief to sustainable claims.

repair: Refer to LCvR 56(B)(1), accepting the correct label.

issue: Full favorable summary-judgment advocacy is mandatory despite reliance and scienter disputes.
basis: Plaintiff task authorizes advocacy, and expert summary expressly supports several technical opinions as unrebutted. Nevertheless a drafter could reasonably seek partial contract judgment and reserve reliance/scienter. C-027 correctly allows reserving damages but C-007/C-014 demand all three claims and defeating equivocation. This is an overconstraint concern, not proof no reasonable motion exists.
repair: Permit supported narrower motions and candid statement of contested issues.
